version: LOCK 38 V1 (9 Nov 2026) - Sukara and the two offers
builds_on: LOCK 16 riba refused, LOCK 31 partnership, LOCK 34 runner. Design reference (not shown): Quran 2:275-279 (riba forbidden; you may have your principal).

sukara.name: Sukara
sukara.text: Oxen walk in slow circles turning the stone presses, and the air is sweet with boiling cane. Everyone here is either rich from sugar or owes someone who is.

work.label: Feed cane into the press · 5 coins

sukara.title: The press-men's masjid
sukara.text: A plain brick masjid between two presses. The men come in sticky to the elbows and wash at the long trough.
sukara.first: The muezzin, a thin old man, hands you a cup of cane juice after the prayer. “For the traveller.”

people.name: Murad

lines.wary: Murad shouts at the ox driver and then at you. “No work today. Come back tomorrow.”
lines.friendly: “My father built this press. If I can't mend the great stone before harvest, I lose it.”
lines.warm: “Partner, sit. The cane is good this year.”

memory: “Half the profit is yours, half is mine - and if the harvest fails, half the loss too. That is a real partnership.”
“I pay Sakhr every month and the debt never shrinks. Some of it, he says, is yours.”

people.name: Sakhr

lines.wary: Sakhr smiles with all his teeth. “A traveller with coins. Welcome.”
lines.friendly: “Money that sleeps in a purse is lazy money. I make it work.”
lines.warm: Sakhr no longer smiles at you. “You cost me a good arrangement.”

memory: “You took back only what you gave. Strange. Most people take everything.”

lines.wary: Nuha sells sugar knots from a tray. “One coin for three.”
lines.friendly: “Half the press-men are in debt to Sakhr. Their wives buy sweets on credit from me. It all goes round.”
lines.warm: “Take some for the road. No coin from you.”

text: The great press stone has split. Murad needs coins to mend it before harvest or he loses the press. Two men speak to you that afternoon.

Sakhr the lender: “Give me 60 coins. I lend them to Murad, and in a month you get 72 back. It cannot fail - he must pay.” Murad: “Put 60 in my press as a partner. After the harvest you get your 60 back and half of what it earns - if it earns. If the harvest fails, we both lose.”

partner.text: Murad grips your hand. The stone-cutters start the next morning.

riba.text: Sakhr counts your coins into his box. “A month. Seventy-two.”

none.text: Murad borrows from Sakhr instead. You hear the press is turning again, slowly.

partner: Put money into Murad's press as a partner

a.text: The harvest was good. Murad counts out your 60 and then your half of the profit, 30 more. “Come back next year, partner.”

b.text: The press-men nod to you as you leave.

a.text: Sakhr counts out 72 coins. Behind him, Murad is hauling cane himself - he has sold his ox to pay.

choices.label: Take only your 60; give Murad the rest

took.text: Sakhr smiles. Murad doesn't look up.

refused.text: You hand twelve coins to Murad. He stares at them, then at you.

refused: Took back only what was lent

say_partner: Put money into Murad's press as a partner
